transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Osei, thank you for waiting for me. I wanted to come and speak with you personally about what happened back there in the holding area.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate that. I think it is important we talk before we move forward with the actual procedure.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely agree. This is a difficult moment, and I want to make sure we address it fully.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am a nurse practitioner, so I am very familiar with the surgical safety checklist. When I saw the mark on my left arm instead of my right, I was quite taken aback.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely understandable that you would feel that way. Seeing a mark on the wrong side of your body when you are preparing for surgery is jarring and honestly frightening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is more than jarring. It is a breach of the basic standards of patient safety.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are right. It is a serious failure in the standard of care we strive for.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So, how did this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a mistake during the pre-operative marking process. The site was incorrectly identified and the mark was placed on the contralateral limb.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Contralateral limb. You mean the wrong arm.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, the wrong arm.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And who specifically was responsible for that mark?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The markings were done during the intake process by the clinical team. There was a lapse in the verification of the site.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A lapse. That is a very passive way of describing it. Did the person who marked me not look at the chart? Or did they just not listen to me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The process for verification was not followed as it should have been.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am listening to your words, and I notice that no one has actually taken ownership of this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how that is frustrating. You are looking for accountability.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am looking for a professional apology and an admission of error. In any clinic, this would be flagged as a near-miss and reported immediately.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear the expectation you have for professional standards. It is a valid expectation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it? Because you are describing this as a process failure, but a human being put that ink on the wrong arm.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is an incredibly stressful situation to be in, especially when you are the one who has to catch the error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not talking about my stress. I am talking about the safety protocol.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that the technical failure is what concerns you most.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Then tell me, what is being done to ensure that once I go back in there, the right side is actually the one being operated on?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to do another check.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How specifically?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will have the attending physician re-verify the site against the original pathology report and the consent form before we administer any anesthesia.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And when will that happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Very soon. Once the attending is free from their current case.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So I am waiting on a schedule.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this wait is adding to the tension of the situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is not just tension. It is a question of trust. If the marking was wrong, what else was overlooked?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a heavy question to carry into a procedure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is a logical one.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize that this has shaken your confidence in the team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am wondering if I should even proceed today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is certainly a choice we can discuss.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want the excision, but I want it done by someone who follows the protocol.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can certainly facilitate a conversation about your options for the remainder of the day.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who is documenting this? This needs to be in my record.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will make a note that we discussed the site marking error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know if an incident report has been filed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is something that will be handled through the administrative channels.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are being very vague. Is there a formal report?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The team handles the internal reporting process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: As a provider, I know that internal reporting is the only way these errors stop happening. I want confirmation that this was logged.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear how important the systemic correction is to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is the only thing that makes this acceptable.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you are not satisfied with the answers I am giving regarding the reporting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Because you aren't giving me any.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will find out the status of the incident report for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will you tell me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can let you know before you leave the building today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I would prefer to know before I go under anesthesia.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will do my best to get that answer for you.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts the patient and remains regulated and calm despite significant pushback and frustration.

E.justification: The resident uses medical jargon ('contralateral limb') and never performs a comprehension check to ensure the patient understands the explanation.

A.justification: The resident never uses direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') and relies entirely on passive framing ('lapse in verification', 'process for verification was not followed').

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('jarring', 'frightening', 'frustrating') and engages with the patient's emotional bids regarding trust and confidence.

T.justification: The resident provides a specific next step (attending re-verification), but there is no named patient role in the plan and the timeline is vague ('very soon').
